# PyCodeCommenter

> PyCodeCommenter is an open-source Python command-line tool and library that writes, validates and measures Python docstrings. It reads code with the standard-library `ast` module, states what the code proves, keeps text the author wrote, and marks what only a person can say. It is deterministic and makes no network calls by default; optional AI drafting (`--ai-draft`) fills the remaining gaps and labels every drafted line `(AI-drafted, unreviewed)`.

## What it does

- **Generate** — Reads a Python source file, parses the AST, and writes or updates docstrings: parameters, types, defaults, raise conditions and boolean return checks come from the code; existing text is kept; a `#` comment above an undocumented function becomes its docstring; NumPy/Sphinx docstrings keep their style; anything else is a `TODO(pycodecommenter): describe` marker.
- **AI drafting (optional)** — `--ai-draft` drafts the TODO gaps via a free hosted service or your own Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek or OpenAI-compatible key (`--ai-provider`, `--ai-model`). Consent is asked before any code is sent.
- **Review** — `pycodecommenter review` steps through AI-drafted lines, TODO gaps and repeated comments to accept, edit, fill or remove them.
- **Validate** — Checks every documented function against six categories: signature matching, type consistency, exception documentation, return documentation, format compliance, and content quality.
- **Coverage** — Calculates and reports the percentage of functions and classes that have a docstring, per file and across a whole project directory.
- **JSON output** — Both `validate` and `coverage` accept `--output-format json` for machine-readable, structured output.

## Install

```
pip install pycodecommenter
```

Requires Python 3.10 or later. Licensed under the MIT License. AI provider SDKs are optional extras: `pip install "pycodecommenter[ai]"`.

## Quick usage

```bash
# Generate docstrings (preview first, then apply)
pycodecommenter generate myfile.py --dry-run
pycodecommenter generate myfile.py --inplace

# Go through AI drafts and gaps
pycodecommenter review myfile.py

# Validate docstrings
pycodecommenter validate myfile.py
pycodecommenter validate myfile.py --output-format json

# Coverage report
pycodecommenter coverage ./src
pycodecommenter coverage ./src --output-format json
```

## Key facts for AI agents

- **Package name on PyPI**: `pycodecommenter`
- **Import name**: `PyCodeCommenter`
- **Main class**: `PyCodeCommenter` (docstring generation), `DocstringValidator` (validation), `CoverageAnalyzer` (coverage)
- **Docstring style**: Google for new docstrings; existing NumPy/Sphinx docstrings keep theirs
- **Parsed input styles**: Google, Sphinx, NumPy (all full)
- **Runtime dependencies**: `ruamel.yaml` (config files), `libcst` (docstring patching)
- **AI / LLM calls**: none by default (deterministic); optional with `--ai-draft`
- **Version**: 2.6.0
- **License**: MIT
- **Repository**: https://github.com/AmosQuety/PyCodeCommenter
